title: INSTEAD OF Triggers on Complex Views
description: Make complex multi-table views fully updatable and intercept writes using INSTEAD OF triggers.

data.text: While simple single-table views are automatically updatable, complex views containing `JOIN`s, aggregates, or `UNION`s are read-only. An **`INSTEAD OF` trigger** intercepts `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` statements on the view and redirects mutations to the underlying base tables.

data.title: Making a User Profile View Updatable
data.content: Splitting writes to users and profiles tables.

data.text: An `INSTEAD OF` trigger replaces the write against the view. You handle each operation the view exposes and decide what to do with the underlying tables. `TG_OP` tells you which statement arrived, and `OLD`/`NEW` carry the rows for `UPDATE` and `DELETE`.

data.title: An updatable join view
data.content: The view joins customers and their addresses; the trigger routes each write to the correct base table.

data.title: Interview angle: when to prefer a view trigger
data.text: `INSTEAD OF` triggers let legacy applications keep writing to a familiar view while the schema underneath is normalized. That is the main legitimate use. The cost is that all the write logic now lives in the trigger, which is invisible to the application and harder to test. If you control the application, updating it to write to the correct tables is usually cleaner than hiding the routing in a trigger.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `INSTEAD OF` triggers apply strictly to Views, not physical tables.
They intercept mutations and redirect writes to underlying relational tables.
Provides clean data abstraction for legacy systems.
